notes.anchor: Skipping Attacks in Message Forwarding Protocols
notes.html:
TODO: add these two entries, numbered by first citation: [23] is cited in the liveness-scope paragraph added after p. 11, [24] in the rewritten Sec. VII (Related Work):

[23] M. Backes, J. Dreier, S. Kremer, and R. Künnemann, “A Novel Approach for Reasoning about Liveness in Cryptographic Protocols and its Application to Fair Exchange,” in IEEE European Symposium on Security and Privacy (EuroS&P), 2017.

[24] A. Kiayias and O. S. T. Litos, “A Composable Security Treatment of the Lightning Network,” in 2020 IEEE 33rd Computer Security Foundations Symposium (CSF), 2020.

TODO: complete these entries from the publishers’ records: [9] has a broken author list (“G. , R. Stefański, …”); [10] lacks the journal; [11] has a garbled page range (“15 pp.–154”); [14] and [22] lack the venue.

Unless stated otherwise, every lemma below is verified in lightning.spthy, the main model (channel layer, multi-hop routing in which one generic rule Forward_HTLC serves every hop of a route of any length, and the wormhole rule AttackerSkip). Lemmas of the auxiliary models are verified in lightning_aux.spthy, one model per preprocessor flag (-D=PTLC, -D=HTLC, -D=CLOCK, -D=CLTV, -D=TIMEOUT). Every listing is copied verbatim from these files with the proof script omitted; listing line numbers refer to lightning.spthy. Sections A–I follow groups 1–9 of Table II and Section K group 0; the lemmas not printed below are given at the end of this appendix (additions to Sections A–H, and Sections I–K).

All results were obtained with Tamarin 1.10 and are reproduced by make all: make verify proves all 55 lemmas of the full model, i.e. with all nine restrictions, including the liveness restrictions T1, T2b and T3, in place (32 all-traces safety lemmas, 13 hop-bypass lemmas, 9 exists-trace lemmas found automatically, and Wormhole_Fee_Theft_Reachable, replayed from a saved 116-step proof); make general proves the 24 lemmas of the any-length theorem in the model without the three liveness restrictions; make aux proves the 21 lemmas of lightning_aux.spthy; make necessity removes one liveness restriction at a time.

notes.anchor: Throughout, action facts carry their intended meaning
notes.html: Throughout, action facts carry their intended meaning from Sec. III (y = h(x) is a payment hash, ptr a channel): InvoiceCreated(R, S, y) — receiver R issued an invoice for y to sender S (the invoice <'invoice', R, S, y> is signed by R and carries no amount); SecretPreimage(R, x) / PreimageReleased(R, x) — R generated / released the preimage x; HTLCOffered(S, F1, ptr, y) — the sender offered an HTLC on y to its first forwarder F1 on channel ptr; OfferFor(S, R, ptr, y) — annotation of the same step naming the invoice’s receiver R; HTLCAdded(ptr, y) — an HTLC on y was added to channel ptr (by an offer or a forward); HTLCForwarded(Me, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) — forwarder Me, holding an incoming HTLC from Prev on ptrIn, added an outgoing HTLC to Next on ptrOut (one rule for every hop); FeeCharged(Me, y, %fee) — the fee Me charges at that forward; HTLCFulfilled(R, Prev, ptr, y) — the receiver redeemed its incoming HTLC; IntermediaryClaimed(Me, Prev, ptrIn, x) / FeeEarned(Me, ptrIn, ptrOut, y, %fee) — forwarder Me redeemed its incoming HTLC with x / earned its fee; SenderSettled(S, F1, R, ptr, x) — the sender settled its HTLC with x; Redeemed(ptr, y) / Refunded(Up, ptr, y) — the HTLC on ptr was redeemed / refunded, after its timeout, to Up, the party that had offered it; TimedOut(ptr) — the HTLC timeout of channel ptr was reached; SettledHop(ptrIn, ptrOut, y) / RefundHop(ptrIn, ptrOut, y) — annotations: the hop from ptrIn to ptrOut settled / had its outgoing HTLC refunded; UsedFulfilled(ptr, x) — annotation: a settlement consumed the fulfilment of the HTLC on ptr; FulfilledProduced(ptr, x) — a fulfilment for ptr was produced by an intermediary settlement or by a skip; Skipped(ptr, x) — annotation of AttackerSkip: compromised parties relayed x onto ptr (wormhole); ChannelOpen(A, B, ptr) — A and B opened channel ptr; KeyGen(A, ltk) — A generated its long-term key ltk; LtkCompromised(A) — A’s long-term key was compromised; K(x) — the adversary knows the term x.

Description unchanged; the invoice carries no amount.

csf_final (lightning.spthy, l. 592):

lemma Invoice_Authenticates_Settlement:
    "All S F1 R ptr x #i.
        SenderSettled(S, F1, R, ptr, x) @ #i
     ==> (Ex #j. InvoiceCreated(R, S, h(x)) @ #j & #j < #i)
       | (Ex #r. LtkCompromised(R) @ #r & #r < #i)"

Statement unchanged; TODO: renumber the listing to lightning.spthy l. 542–547. Add: In this model the preimage is never sent to the network: fulfilments travel between hops as state facts, and AttackerSkip relays them without the adversary learning x. Hence Preimage_Never_Known (additions to Sec. A) holds, and this lemma holds trivially.

Reachability witness. There is a trace in which the sender settles an HTLC for receiver R although R never created an invoice for h(x); R’s long-term key is compromised in this trace, and no forwarding takes place. Together with Lemma 5, which requires such a compromise to precede the settlement, this shows that the compromise case of Lemma 5 is not vacuous.

csf_final (lightning.spthy, l. 598):

lemma Forged_Invoice_Requires_Key_Compromise:
    exists-trace
    "Ex S F1 R ptr x #i #r.
        SenderSettled(S, F1, R, ptr, x) @ #i
      & LtkCompromised(R) @ #r
      & not (Ex #j. InvoiceCreated(R, S, h(x)) @ #j)
      & not (Ex Me Prev Next pi po y #u. HTLCForwarded(Me, Prev, Next, pi, po, y) @ #u)"

Statement unchanged; TODO: renumber the listing to lightning.spthy l. 508–512. New justification: This holds because Receiver_Fulfill_HTLC consumes the linear fact ReceiverInv(R, S, x), which Receiver_Create_Invoice creates once per fresh preimage x.

Lemma (Forward_Requires_Incoming (∀)). A forwarder adds an outgoing HTLC only if an HTLC on the same hash was added earlier to its incoming channel, either offered to it by a sender or forwarded to it by its predecessor. The lemma covers every hop of a route of any length and needs no honesty assumption.

Statement (lightning.spthy, l. 576):

lemma Forward_Requires_Incoming [use_induction]:
    "All Me Prev Next ptrIn ptrOut y #i.
        HTLCForwarded(Me, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #i
     ==> (Ex S #j. HTLCOffered(S, Me, ptrIn, y) @ #j & #j < #i)
       | (Ex P0 pin0 #j. HTLCForwarded(Prev, P0, Me, pin0, ptrIn, y) @ #j & #j < #i)"
Statement unchanged; TODO: renumber the listing to lightning.spthy l. 554–557. HTLCAdded is emitted by Sender_Offer_HTLC and Forward_HTLC.
Statement unchanged; TODO: renumber the listing to lightning.spthy l. 570–574 and write its first line as lemma Claim_Requires_Release [use_induction]:.

notes.anchor: a settlement never precedes the receiver's release
notes.html:
Lemma 14: description unchanged; the invoice carries no amount.

csf_final (lightning.spthy, l. 564):

lemma Settle_Requires_Receiver_Release:
    "All S F1 R ptr x #i #j.
        SenderSettled(S, F1, R, ptr, x) @ #i
      & InvoiceCreated(R, S, h(x)) @ #j
     ==> Ex #k. PreimageReleased(R, x) @ #k & #k < #i"

If two forwarders F1 and F2 forward consecutive HTLCs on the same hash y (the outgoing channel of F1 is the incoming channel of F2), the HTLC on F2’s outgoing channel is redeemed, and no party’s long-term key is ever compromised, then the HTLC on F1’s incoming channel is never refunded: in a run without any key compromise, once the payment is redeemed downstream of two forwarders, the party upstream of them cannot be refunded. The lemma is proved in the full model, i.e. under the liveness restrictions; it also verifies with T1 removed (Table III).

csf_final (lightning.spthy, l. 625):

lemma Payment_Atomicity_Under_Liveness:
    "All F1 F2 Prev1 Next1 Prev2 Next2 ptrSF1 ptrF1F2 ptrF2R y #i #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(F1, Prev1, Next1, ptrSF1, ptrF1F2, y) @ #i
      & HTLCForwarded(F2, Prev2, Next2, ptrF1F2, ptrF2R, y) @ #j
      & Redeemed(ptrF2R, y) @ #k
      & (not Ex P #l. LtkCompromised(P) @ #l)
     ==> not (Ex Up #m. Refunded(Up, ptrSF1, y) @ #m)"

TODO: in the description replace “can never be refunded later” by “is never refunded” (the statement excludes a refund at any time).

csf_final (lightning.spthy, l. 587):

lemma Settle_Excludes_Sender_Refund [heuristic={sender_pending}]:
    "All S F1 R ptr x #i.
        SenderSettled(S, F1, R, ptr, x) @ #i
     ==> not (Ex #j. Refunded(S, ptr, h(x)) @ #j)"

Replace Lemma 17 by two non-vacuity witnesses.

Lemma (Multihop_Routing_Reachable (∃)). The routing phase of a payment over two forwarders is reachable: the sender offers, both forwarders forward and the receiver fulfils, with no other offer or forward, at most one HTLC per channel, and no intermediary claim or sender settlement.

Statement (lightning.spthy, l. 644):

lemma Multihop_Routing_Reachable:
    exists-trace
    "Ex S F1 F2 R p0 p1 p2 x #t2 #t3 #t4 #t5.
        HTLCOffered(S, F1, p0, h(x)) @ #t2
      & HTLCForwarded(F1, S, F2, p0, p1, h(x)) @ #t3
      & HTLCForwarded(F2, F1, R, p1, p2, h(x)) @ #t4
      & HTLCFulfilled(R, F2, p2, h(x)) @ #t5
      & #t2 < #t3 & #t3 < #t4 & #t4 < #t5
      & not (Ex A B p y #u. HTLCOffered(A, B, p, y) @ #u & not (A = S & B = F1))
      & not (Ex Me Prev Next pi po y #u. HTLCForwarded(Me, Prev, Next, pi, po, y) @ #u
              & not (Me = F1 & Prev = S & Next = F2)
              & not (Me = F2 & Prev = F1 & Next = R))
      & not (Ex ptr y1 y2 #m #n. HTLCAdded(ptr, y1) @ #m & HTLCAdded(ptr, y2) @ #n & not (#m = #n))
      & not (Ex Me P q z #e. IntermediaryClaimed(Me, P, q, z) @ #e)
      & not (Ex A B C q z #e. SenderSettled(A, B, C, q, z) @ #e)"

Lemma (Sanity_Atomic_Payment_Completes (∃)). An honest payment over two forwarders completes end to end: offer, both forwards, fulfilment, both intermediary claims and the sender’s settlement occur, with no key compromise, at most one HTLC per channel, exactly these claims and this settlement, and no refund. It shows that the premise of Lemma 15 is satisfiable.

Statement (lightning.spthy, l. 1123):

lemma Sanity_Atomic_Payment_Completes:
  exists-trace
  "Ex S F1 F2 R p0 p1 p2 x #o #a #b #r #c1 #c2 #s.
      HTLCOffered(S, F1, p0, h(x)) @ #o
    & HTLCForwarded(F1, S, F2, p0, p1, h(x)) @ #a
    & HTLCForwarded(F2, F1, R, p1, p2, h(x)) @ #b
    & HTLCFulfilled(R, F2, p2, h(x)) @ #r
    & IntermediaryClaimed(F2, F1, p1, x) @ #c2
    & IntermediaryClaimed(F1, S, p0, x) @ #c1
    & SenderSettled(S, F1, R, p0, x) @ #s
    & not (Ex P #k. LtkCompromised(P) @ #k)
    & not (Ex ptr y1 y2 #m #n. HTLCAdded(ptr, y1) @ #m & HTLCAdded(ptr, y2) @ #n & not (#m = #n))
    & (All Me P q z #e. IntermediaryClaimed(Me, P, q, z) @ #e ==> (#e = #c1 | #e = #c2))
    & (All A B C q z #e. SenderSettled(A, B, C, q, z) @ #e ==> #e = #s)
    & not (Ex U q z #e. Refunded(U, q, z) @ #e)"

TODO: retitle the subsection “E. Fees” and replace Lemmas 18–24 by the following text.

Amounts are local to a hop: Forward_HTLC receives the incoming amount, the fee and the outgoing amount as inputs and emits Eq(%vIn, %vOut %+ %fee), which the Equality restriction enforces, so per-hop value conservation holds by construction. The offer, the invoice and the route carry no amount, so amounts are not chained along the path and the model makes no end-to-end value statement. The fee guarantee is Fee_Only_On_Successful_Forward (Additions to E, end of this appendix): an uncompromised forwarder earns its fee only after its outgoing HTLC was redeemed.

Description unchanged.

csf_final (lightning.spthy, l. 613):

lemma Refund_Requires_Timeout [reuse]:
    "All Up ptr y #i.
        Refunded(Up, ptr, y) @ #i
     ==> Ex #j. TimedOut(ptr) @ #j & #j < #i"

TODO: in the description replace “is never redeemed afterwards” by “is never redeemed” (the statement excludes a redemption at any time).

csf_final (lightning.spthy, l. 606):

lemma Loss_Requires_Inaction:
    "All P Prev Next Up ptrIn ptrOut y #i #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #i
      & Redeemed(ptrOut, y) @ #j
      & Refunded(Up, ptrIn, y) @ #k
     ==> not (Ex #l. Redeemed(ptrIn, y) @ #l)"

TODO: keep the title “F. Refund and Griefing” (group 6 of the new Table II, “Refund / griefing”). lightning.spthy has no counterpart of Lemma 27 (an honest forwarder whose outgoing HTLC is refunded with no settlement anywhere). The refund witness of the model is the weaker Refund_Possible, which Sec. V-E reports as reachable griefing of the sender: its HTLC stays locked until the timeout (Refund_Requires_Timeout):

Lemma (Refund_Possible (∃)). A payment can be refunded: the receiver issues an invoice, the sender offers an HTLC on its hash, and the sender’s HTLC is refunded after its timeout, with no settlement, no key compromise, no forwarding, and at most one HTLC per channel.

Statement (lightning.spthy, l. 530):

lemma Refund_Possible:
    exists-trace
    "Ex S F1 R p y #i #j #k.
        InvoiceCreated(R, S, y) @ #j
      & HTLCOffered(S, F1, p, y) @ #k
      & Refunded(S, p, y) @ #i
      & #j < #k & #k < #i
      & not (Ex A MidP B p2 x #l. SenderSettled(A, MidP, B, p2, x) @ #l)
      & not (Ex P #r. LtkCompromised(P) @ #r)
      & not (Ex Me Prev Next pi po y2 #t1. HTLCForwarded(Me, Prev, Next, pi, po, y2) @ #t1)
      & not (Ex ptr y1 y2 #m #n. HTLCAdded(ptr, y1) @ #m & HTLCAdded(ptr, y2) @ #n & not (#m = #n))"

Reachability witness (attack). There is a trace on the route Alice → Att1 → Indiana → Att2 → Bob in which Bob issues the invoice and redeems his incoming HTLC and Alice settles her HTLC, yet the outgoing HTLC of the intermediary Indiana is refunded and Indiana earns no fee. Alice, Bob and Indiana are never compromised, and Att1 and Att2 are distinct parties. This is the wormhole [6]: the preimage is relayed around Indiana by rule AttackerSkip, which only two compromised parties on the same payment can apply. Tamarin does not find this trace automatically: make verify replays a saved 116-step proof. In the PTLC model of Section J the corresponding wormhole around an honest hop is unreachable (No_Wormhole_Around_Honest_Hop), while the HTLC baseline reaches it (Wormhole_Around_Honest_Hop).

csf_final (lightning.spthy, l. 660):

lemma Wormhole_Fee_Theft_Reachable:
  exists-trace
  "∃ Alice Bob Att1 Att2 Indiana ptrAliceAtt1 ptrAtt1Indiana
     ptrIndianaAtt2 ptrAtt2Bob x #t1 #t2 #t3 #t4 #t5 #t6 #t7 #t8.
    (((((((((((((((InvoiceCreated( Bob, Alice, h(x) ) @ #t1) ∧
                  (HTLCOffered( Alice, Att1, ptrAliceAtt1, h(x) ) @ #t2)) ∧
                 (HTLCForwarded( Att1, Alice, Indiana, ptrAliceAtt1, ptrAtt1Indiana,
                                 h(x)
                  ) @ #t3)) ∧
                (HTLCForwarded( Indiana, Att1, Att2, ptrAtt1Indiana,
                                ptrIndianaAtt2, h(x)
                 ) @ #t4)) ∧
               (HTLCForwarded( Att2, Indiana, Bob, ptrIndianaAtt2, ptrAtt2Bob,
                               h(x)
                ) @ #t5)) ∧
              (HTLCFulfilled( Bob, Att2, ptrAtt2Bob, h(x) ) @ #t6)) ∧
             (SenderSettled( Alice, Att1, Bob, ptrAliceAtt1, x ) @ #t7)) ∧
            (Refunded( Indiana, ptrIndianaAtt2, h(x) ) @ #t8)) ∧
           (¬(Indiana = Alice))) ∧
          (¬(Indiana = Bob))) ∧
         (¬(Att1 = Att2))) ∧
        (¬(∃ #c. LtkCompromised( Alice ) @ #c))) ∧
       (¬(∃ #c. LtkCompromised( Bob ) @ #c))) ∧
      (¬(∃ #c. LtkCompromised( Indiana ) @ #c))) ∧
     (¬(∃ ptr1 ptr2 yy %fee #k.
         FeeEarned( Indiana, ptr1, ptr2, yy, %fee ) @ #k))) ∧
    (¬(∃ ptr y1 y2 #m #n.
        ((HTLCAdded( ptr, y1 ) @ #m) ∧ (HTLCAdded( ptr, y2 ) @ #n)) ∧
        (¬(#m = #n))))"

Lemma 30, replacement for the struck sentence: Equivalently, an honest intermediary whose outgoing HTLC is redeemed never has its incoming HTLC refunded. The stronger Intermediary_Never_Loses_Strong (Additions to H) places the compromise before the incoming timeout.

csf_final (lightning.spthy, l. 618):

lemma Intermediary_Never_Loses_Under_Liveness:
    "All P Prev Next Up ptrIn ptrOut y #i #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #i
      & Redeemed(ptrOut, y) @ #j
      & Refunded(Up, ptrIn, y) @ #k
     ==> Ex #l. LtkCompromised(P) @ #l"

No intermediary that is not compromised before its incoming timeout has its incoming HTLC refunded when that timeout happens strictly before its outgoing HTLC is redeemed. The lemma also verifies with any one of T1, T2b and T3 removed (4 steps each, Table III), so it does not depend on any single liveness restriction. In the abstract TIMEOUT model of lightning_aux.spthy, where either channel may time out at any point and the outgoing HTLC may be redeemed at any time, the race is reachable (Early_Timeout_Race, ∃, 6 steps).

csf_final (lightning.spthy, l. 633):

lemma Timeout_Race_Blocked:
    "not (Ex P Prev Next Up ptrIn ptrOut y #l #i #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #l
      & TimedOut(ptrIn)     @ #k
      & Refunded(Up, ptrIn, y)  @ #j
      & Redeemed(ptrOut, y) @ #i
      & #k < #i
      & not (Ex #c. LtkCompromised(P) @ #c & #c < #k))"

inserts.title: Appendix A additions: csf_final lemmas missing from the catalogue
inserts.html:
The following lemmas complete the catalogue; the section letters follow the groups of Table II. Statements are verbatim (proof scripts omitted); ∀ = all-traces, ∃ = exists-trace. Unless a flag is given they belong to lightning.spthy and are proved by make verify.

Additions to A (Invoice and Preimage)

Preimage_Never_Known (∀) [lightning.spthy, l. 1141]. The adversary never learns a receiver’s preimage (x is never output in this model); Lemma 6 therefore holds trivially.

lemma Preimage_Never_Known:
    "All R x #i. SecretPreimage(R, x) @ #i ==> not (Ex #j. K(x) @ #j)"

Invoice_Has_Secret_Preimage (∀) [lightning.spthy, l. 549]. Every invoice is created together with the receiver’s secret preimage of its hash.

lemma Invoice_Has_Secret_Preimage [reuse]:
    "All R S x #i.
        InvoiceCreated(R, S, h(x)) @ #i
     ==> SecretPreimage(R, x) @ #i"

Additions to B (Lock Causality)

Offer_Requires_Invoice (∀) [lightning.spthy, l. 1115]. An HTLC is offered for receiver R only against an invoice that R created earlier, or R’s long-term key is compromised.

lemma Offer_Requires_Invoice:
    "All S R ptr y #o.
        OfferFor(S, R, ptr, y) @ #o
     ==> (Ex #j. InvoiceCreated(R, S, y) @ #j & #j < #o)
       | (Ex #r. LtkCompromised(R) @ #r)"

Additions to C (Release Causality)

Fulfilled_Requires_Release (∀) [lightning.spthy, l. 559]. Every fulfilment produced by an intermediary settlement or a skip is preceded by a receiver’s release of x.

lemma Fulfilled_Requires_Release [reuse, use_induction, heuristic=S]:
    "All ptr x #i.
        FulfilledProduced(ptr, x) @ #i
     ==> Ex R #k. PreimageReleased(R, x) @ #k & #k < #i"

Redeem_Requires_Receiver_Release (∀) [lightning.spthy, l. 582]. Every redeemed HTLC on y comes with a receiver’s release of a preimage x with h(x) = y.

lemma Redeem_Requires_Receiver_Release [use_induction]:
    "All ptr y #i.
        Redeemed(ptr, y) @ #i
     ==> Ex R x #k. PreimageReleased(R, x) @ #k & h(x) = y"

Fulfilled_Source (∀) [lightning.spthy, l. 1148]. A fulfilment consumed by a settlement stems from an earlier redemption of that HTLC or from an earlier skip.

lemma Fulfilled_Source [reuse]:
    "All p x #i. UsedFulfilled(p, x) @ #i
     ==> (Ex #j. Redeemed(p, h(x)) @ #j & #j < #i)
       | (Ex #j. Skipped(p, x) @ #j & #j < #i)"

Additions to D (Atomicity)

OneOutcomePerHTLC (∀) [lightning.spthy, l. 498]. No HTLC is both redeemed and refunded.

lemma OneOutcomePerHTLC [reuse]:
    "All Up ptr y #i #j.
       Redeemed(ptr, y) @ #i & Refunded(Up, ptr, y) @ #j ==> F"

Sanity_Honest_Payment_Completes (∃) [lightning.spthy, l. 1075]. An honest payment over one forwarder completes end to end, with no compromise and no refund.

lemma Sanity_Honest_Payment_Completes:
  exists-trace
  "Ex S F1 R p0 p1 x #o #a #r #c #s.

Additions to H (Intermediary Safety, Timing)

ForwardTimeGap (∀) [lightning.spthy, l. 426]. If both channels of a forward time out and the forwarder is not compromised before its incoming timeout, the outgoing HTLC times out strictly before the incoming one. T2a is not a restriction in this model: it is this lemma, derived from T2b. Under -D=NECESSITY it is declared without [reuse].

lemma ForwardTimeGap [reuse]:
    "All P Prev Next ptrIn ptrOut y #f #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #f
      & TimedOut(ptrOut) @ #j
      & TimedOut(ptrIn)  @ #k
      & not (Ex #c. LtkCompromised(P) @ #c & #c < #k)
     ==> #j < #k"

Intermediary_Never_Loses_Strong (∀) [lightning.spthy, l. 1106]. A forwarder whose outgoing HTLC is redeemed while its incoming HTLC is refunded was compromised before its incoming HTLC timed out.

lemma Intermediary_Never_Loses_Strong:
    "All P Prev Next Up ptrIn ptrOut y #i #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #i
      & Redeemed(ptrOut, y) @ #j
      & Refunded(Up, ptrIn, y) @ #k
     ==> Ex #l #t. LtkCompromised(P) @ #l & TimedOut(ptrIn) @ #t & #l < #t"

    & Refunded(S, p0, h(x)) @ #u
    & LtkCompromised(F1) @ #k
    & not (Ex ptr y1 y2 #m #n. HTLCAdded(ptr, y1) @ #m & HTLCAdded(ptr, y2) @ #n & not (#m = #n))

    & not (Ex A B C q z #e. SenderSettled(A, B, C, q, z) @ #e)"

I. Hop Bypass: Skipping a Forwarder Requires a Compromise

If the payment settles at the sender while a forwarder’s own hop is refunded, some party’s key was compromised. The conclusion does not say which party, or when. The lemmas for positions 1–6 need no single-offer premise; Any_Hop_Skip_Requires_Compromise covers any position on a route of any length under a single-offer premise (every offer on h(x) uses the sender’s channel pSF).

First_Hop_Skip_Requires_Compromise (∀) [lightning.spthy, l. 1208]. The first forwarder cannot be bypassed without a compromise.

lemma First_Hop_Skip_Requires_Compromise [heuristic={lemmas_first}]:
    "All S F1 R pSF Next pOut x #s #f #r.
        SenderSettled(S, F1, R, pSF, x) @ #s
      & HTLCForwarded(F1, S, Next, pSF, pOut, h(x)) @ #f
      & RefundHop(pSF, pOut, h(x)) @ #r
     ==> Ex P #c. LtkCompromised(P) @ #c"

      & HTLCForwarded(F1, S, F2, pSF, p1, h(x)) @ #f1
      & HTLCForwarded(F2, F1, Next, p1, pOut, h(x)) @ #f2
      & RefundHop(p1, pOut, h(x)) @ #r
     ==> Ex P #c. LtkCompromised(P) @ #c"

Any_Hop_Skip_Requires_Compromise (∀) — make general (-D=GENERAL -D=NO_IMC -D=NO_OTF -D=NO_RBT -D=NECESSITY), 7 steps [lightning.spthy, l. 1803]. A single-offer payment that settles while any forwarder’s own hop is refunded requires a compromise. Proved in the model without the three liveness restrictions; removing restrictions only adds traces, so the statement also holds in the full model.

lemma Any_Hop_Skip_Requires_Compromise [heuristic={lemmas_first}]:
  all-traces
  "∀ S F1 R pSF x Me Prev Next pIn pOut #s #f #r.
    ((((SenderSettled( S, F1, R, pSF, x ) @ #s) ∧
       (HTLCForwarded( Me, Prev, Next, pIn, pOut, h(x) ) @ #f)) ∧
      (RefundHop( pIn, pOut, h(x) ) @ #r)) ∧
     (∀ A B p #o. (HTLCOffered( A, B, p, h(x) ) @ #o) ⇒ (p = pSF))) ⇒
    (∃ P #c. LtkCompromised( P ) @ #c)"
